To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose GFlowNets, a new type of generative model based on flow networks, and show that it achieves state of the art performance on the molecule synthesis task, (2) we show that GFlowNet can be used to generate diverse solutions, and (3) we show that it can also be used as a black box optimizer, achieving state of the art results on the molecule synthesis and protein folding tasks.

we introduce a new model, GFlowNet, for non-iterative diverse generation, that we show to be theoretically grounded, and that we demonstrate empirically that it outperforms baselines on two challenging domains.

this paper proposes a new approach to learn a generative policy for generating an output from a sequence of decisions (or actions), where the probability of generating a particular output is proportional to its positive reward.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a novel framework for learning a generative model from a black-box reward function that can be used to generate diverse high-reward samples.
we propose a novel generative framework for learning a stochastic policy which is able to generate diverse samples of a target distribution.

we propose GFlow Nets, a new class of models for generative modeling that are based on a view that a generative process can be seen as a flow network and we can train the network to sample from a desired distribution using flow consistency equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show how a flow network based generative model can be used to generate diverse candidates.

the problem of learning to generate diverse high-return trajectories can be cast as an optimization over a certain class of flow networks, and that the resulting GFlowNet can be learned with gradient descent.

we show that it is possible to learn a generative policy which samples from a desired distribution, even when the policy can only take actions that are consistent with the flow of a stochastic process.
